fields.Participants: Procurement, VP Supply Chain, Legal, Finance, CFO
fields.Trigger: Need for new delivery capacity or partner replacement

Automation Opportunity: - Due-diligence checklist auto-assembled per partner; risk-tier auto-suggested from the screening data
Controls: - CTL-06: 3PL vendor-master onboarding; CTL-167 (TPRM risk-tiering — links to VS-161); operational: VP Supply Chain + CFO sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-vetted-partner risk**: insufficient due diligence lets a partner with a poor safety/financial record through; mitigated by the documented due-diligence checklist (DTI/SEC, insurance, references) and the TPRM risk-tiering
- **Over-concentration risk**: too much volume with one partner creates leverage and continuity risk; mitigated by the no-single-partner->50% rule (W2195)
System Touchpoints: - Vendor/partner master (links to VS-03 / W36, VS-62B 3PL onboarding) — the partner record and due-diligence documentation
- Contract repository (links to VS-100 / W230, VS-88) — the 3PL service agreement
- TPRM (links to VS-161 / W4721 third-party risk tiering) — the partner risk assessment
Time Estimate: ~4 days/evaluation × ~3/year = **~96 hours/year** Logistics Manager + Procurement + Legal.

steps.activity: Logistics Manager identifies potential partners based on geographic coverage, vehicle fleet, pricing, and reputation; Procurement conducts due diligence (DTI/SEC registration, insurance, safety record, references)
Legal reviews contract: SLA terms, liability, insurance, data privacy (RA 10173), rate card, payment terms, termination; Finance evaluates pricing and sets up vendor master

fields.Participants: IT, Logistics Manager, CIO, VP Supply Chain

Controls: - CTL-397 (ensure controlled execution — 3PL Partner Onboarding & Qualification (PA-56.1).)
- CTL-397: API/integration integrity — links to VS-27; operational: CIO sign-off on go-live after pilot
Pain Points / Risks: - **Integration-failure risk**: the API integration fails in production (the sandbox didn't catch a real-world condition); mitigated by the 2-week pilot with one DC before full rollout
- **Partner-system-limitation risk**: the partner's system can't support the required integration (no API, manual-only); mitigated by the integration-capability screening at W2190
System Touchpoints: - API/integration (links to VS-27 / W257 enterprise API lifecycle, VS-56 / W2198 tracking) — the 3PL integration
- ERP/order management (links to VS-60 / W536 unified order management, VS-04 / W106 dispatch) — the order-push and status
- IT change management (links to VS-27 / W132) — the integration release

steps.activity: IT configures API integration: order push, delivery status, proof of delivery, driver tracking; tests in sandbox; Logistics Manager trains partner on BuildRight processes
Pilot period: 2-week controlled rollout with 1 DC; monitors performance vs. SLA; full rollout upon meeting pilot criteria

Automation Opportunity: - Credential-expiry auto-tracked; auto-suspension on lapse; re-certification auto-requested 30 days before expiry
Controls: - CTL-397: driver/vehicle compliance — links to VS-167, VS-06; CTL-153 (driver personal-data privacy — links to VS-91); operational: Logistics Manager sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lapsed-credential risk**: a driver's license or drug test expires between annual re-certifications, leaving a non-compliant driver delivering for BuildRight; mitigated by the expiry-tracking with auto-suspension on lapse
- **Privacy risk**: the driver background check and drug test involve personal data; mitigated by the RA 10173-compliant handling (consent, purpose limitation, VS-91)
System Touchpoints: - Driver/vehicle compliance (links to VS-167 / W167 workforce vetting, VS-06 / W197 driver safety) — the credential verification
- TPRM (links to VS-161 / W4721) — the compliance as a third-party-risk dimension
- RA 10173 (links to VS-91 / W53) — the driver personal-data privacy
Time Estimate: ~2.5 days/onboarding + ~1.5 weeks annual re-cert = **~300 hours/year** Logistics Coordinator.

steps.activity: Coordinator verifies driver credentials: professional license, drug test, background check, BuildRight safety training; verifies vehicle compliance: registration, insurance, roadworthiness
Annual re-certification: partners submit updated documents; non-compliant drivers/vehicles suspended until cleared

fields.Frequency: Annual; ad-hoc for fuel price changes
fields.Trigger: Annual rate card review or significant cost change

Controls: - CTL-397: 3PL-contract accuracy — links to VS-03; CTL-48 (rate-dispute resolution); operational: CFO sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Above-market-rate risk**: a partner's rate drifts above market without BuildRight noticing; mitigated by the annual benchmark and the spot-rate comparison

- **Rate-card-complexity risk**: an overly complex rate card (many surcharges, exceptions) makes billing opaque and error-prone; mitigated by the simplified rate-card preference (base + standard surcharges)
System Touchpoints: - Rate card / pricing (links to VS-03 / W62 contract, VS-29 / W304 routing & transit-time master) — the negotiated rates
- Cost analytics (links to VS-61 / W2325 fleet TCO, VS-27 / W113) — the spend and benchmark data
- Fuel-adjustment (links to VS-61 / W2316 fuel pass-through) — the ad-hoc fuel-trigger

steps.activity: Logistics Manager analyzes spend, volume, and market rates; benchmarks vs. spot rates; negotiates: base per-km rate, weight surcharges, waiting time, multi-drop discounts, peak surcharges
Finance validates cost impact; approves; updated rate card configured in ERP

Automation Opportunity: - Insurance-expiry auto-tracked; auto-suspension on lapse; claim auto-filed on incident
Controls: - CTL-397: 3PL insurance adequacy — links to VS-26; CTL-42 (partner-bank-detail guard on settlements); operational: CFO sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lapsed-insurance risk**: a partner's insurance lapses between annual reviews, leaving BuildRight exposed on a delivery incident; mitigated by the expiry-tracking with auto-suspension on lapse
- **Underinsurance risk**: the partner's coverage is below the cargo value, leaving a gap on a total-loss; mitigated by the coverage-vs-cargo-value check
System Touchpoints: - Insurance (links to VS-26 / W59 insurance policy, W610 claims) — the 3PL insurance tracking
- Claims (links to VS-90 / W90 damage claims, VS-53 / W2140 performance guarantee) — the delivery-incident claims
- Partner master (links to VS-03 / W36) — the insurance-expiry tracking
Time Estimate: ~2.5 hours/quarter + ~1 day/year ≈ 10 + 8 hours = **~18–20 hours/year** Logistics Manager + Finance.

steps.activity: Manager ensures all partners maintain required insurance (vehicle, cargo, third-party liability); tracks expiry dates; files claims for incidents (damage, loss, accident)
Annual: reviews insurance adequacy; adjusts coverage based on claims history and delivery volume growth

fields.Trigger: Seasonal capacity review or new store openings

Automation Opportunity: - Capacity-need auto-forecast; allocation auto-suggested per performance/cost
Controls: - CTL-397 (ensure controlled execution — 3PL Partner Onboarding & Qualification (PA-56.1).)
- CTL-397: capacity-plan accuracy; operational: VP Supply Chain sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Capacity-shortfall risk**: a peak exceeds the 3PL capacity, causing delivery delays; mitigated by the quarterly forecast and the surge-capacity pre-booking
- **Over-allocation-to-one risk**: >50% with one partner creates leverage/continuity risk; mitigated by the diversification rule
System Touchpoints: - Capacity forecasting (links to VS-02 / W31 demand forecasting, VS-60 / W2307 fulfillment capacity) — the volume forecast
- Allocation (links to VS-56 / W2196 scorecard) — the performance-based allocation
- DC scheduling (links to VS-04 / W585 dock scheduling) — the surge coordination
Time Estimate: ~2.5 days/quarter + ~1 week surge = **~120 hours/year** Logistics Manager.

steps.activity: Manager forecasts capacity needs: seasonal peaks, new stores (~10–15/year), replenishment volume; allocates across partners by capacity, performance, cost; ensures no single partner >50%
Coordinates surge capacity for peaks: pre-books vehicles, temporary agreements, adjusts DC scheduling

Automation Opportunity: - Scorecard auto-generated; below-target auto-flagged with CAP
Controls: - CTL-397: 3PL performance accuracy; CTL-24 (delivery-fraud detection); operational: COO quarterly portfolio review
Pain Points / Risks: - **Scorecard-without-consequence risk**: below-target partners don't face consequences (the CAP isn't enforced); mitigated by the retention/reallocation decision at the quarterly review
- **Metric-gaming risk**: a partner games a metric (marks "delivered" before actual delivery to hit OTD); mitigated by the POD-verified delivery (W2202) as the ground truth
System Touchpoints: - Scorecard (links to VS-67 / W2458 vendor scorecard, VS-56 / W2199 SLA monitoring) — the 3PL performance data
- Analytics (links to VS-27 / W113) — the scorecard visualization
- Corrective action (links to VS-67 / W2465 PIP pattern) — the below-target CAP

steps.activity: System generates scorecard: on-time delivery rate (≥95%), damage rate (<0.5%), order acceptance rate, avg delivery time, complaint rate, driver professionalism; Manager reviews with partner
Below-target partners get 30-day corrective action plans; quarterly: VP reviews portfolio for retention/reallocation/new sourcing decisions

fields.Participants: Procurement, IT, VP Supply Chain, Finance

Automation Opportunity: - Termination-checklist auto-sequenced; volume-transition auto-coordinated; settlement auto-reconciled
Controls: - CTL-397 (ensure controlled execution — 3PL Partner Onboarding & Qualification (PA-56.1).)
- operational: partner-master status update; final-settlement bank-detail guard; operational: VP Supply Chain sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Transition-disruption risk**: the volume shift causes delivery gaps during the handover; mitigated by the overlap period (new partner ramped up before old fully offboarded)
- **Final-settlement-dispute risk**: the departing partner disputes the final invoice or claims unpaid deliveries; mitigated by the POD-verified settlement (W2202) and the CTL-48 dispute workflow
System Touchpoints: - Contract termination (links to VS-03 / W62B 3PL offboarding, VS-56 / W2190) — the termination process
- Volume transition (links to VS-56 / W2195 capacity allocation) — the reallocation
- Financial settlement (links to VS-15 / W7, VS-56 / W2206 invoice) — the final settlement
Time Estimate: ~45 days/transition × ~1.5/year = **~200 hours/year** Logistics Manager + Procurement + IT + Finance.

steps.activity: Manager initiates termination per contract terms (60–90 days notice); documents justification; Procurement sources replacement; IT begins integration
Executes volume transition over 2–4 weeks; closes financial settlement with departing partner
